question: Point out the INCORRECT response regarding infection by human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and pregnancy:

options.opa: The scheduled cesarean does not reduce the vertical transmission rate of the virus.
options.opb: The pregnant woman will be offered the possibility of performing antiretroviral treatment whatever her stage of the disease, in order to prevent the vertical transmission of the virus.
options.opc: Vertical transmission of the virus is associated with maternal viral load.
options.opd: HIV serology must be offered to every pregnant woman at the first consultation, whatever the time of pregnancy.
options.ope: Women infected with HIV have an increased risk of spontaneous abortions, intrauterine fetal death and intrauterine growth retardation.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Vertical transmission of HIV is associated with maternal viral load -> Maternal viral load affects the risk of transmitting the virus to the fetus -> Maternal viral load is a crucial factor in determining the likelihood of vertical transmission of HIV -> 95%
enhanced_information: The incorrect response is opa. Scheduled cesarean delivery can significantly reduce the vertical transmission rate of HIV. Maternal viral load is a crucial factor in determining the likelihood of vertical transmission of HIV, and antiretroviral treatment is offered to pregnant women to prevent vertical transmission. HIV serology should be offered to every pregnant woman, and women infected with HIV have an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes.
analysis: Scheduled cesarean delivery can significantly reduce the vertical transmission rate of HIV, contrary to the statement in option a. Maternal viral load is indeed associated with vertical transmission risk, and antiretroviral treatment is offered to prevent transmission. HIV serology is recommended for all pregnant women, and HIV infection does increase the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes.
